THE TRAP: a plain OpenZeppelin ERC-20 compiles to near-identical bytecode
for thousands of honest tokens AND for every scammer who never edited the
template. One generic hash in here marks all of them known_bad. Nothing in
code can tell a rug template from a generic one, so each entry MUST carry:
hash     sha256 of the normalised runtime bytecode
example  a contract address that used it and is known to have rugged
note     why this code is DISTINCTIVE — the hidden mint, the blacklist,
the transfer hook — and not just a standard template
The loader refuses any entry missing example or note.
SHIPPED EMPTY, and the empty state is honest: the check answers `unknown`
rather than clearing a contract it never compared against anything.
